_description: Input Range and OVP Test Configuration — SENSOR Board
_objective: Verify both buck regulator outputs (3.3 V and 3.6 V) remain within tolerance across the full specified input voltage operating range (4.5 V – 6.0 V). Each rail is probed in sequence: operator connects DMM to the 3.3 V rail first, all VIN test points are measured, then operator moves DMM to the 3.6 V rail and VIN points are repeated.
_instructions: Edit values below instead of modifying the Python code. Re-run the test to pick up changes.

instrument_addresses._note: VISA address strings for each instrument. Run 'python -m visa_auto_detect' to list detected addresses.

output_dir._note: Base folder for results. A timestamped sub-folder is created automatically for each run.

instrument_settings._note: PSU channel selection (1, 2, or 3) and instrument communication timeouts (milliseconds).

test_parameters._note: Tunable test execution parameters. Sweep settings are kept for compatibility but the SENSOR multi-rail test runs fixed-VIN tests only — no sweep is performed.

output_rails._note: Phase 1: 3.3V buck output. Connect DMM probes to 3V3 rail before this phase begins.
output_rails.name: 3V3
output_rails.label: VOUT 3.3(V)

output_rails._note: Phase 2: 3.6V buck output. Move DMM probes to 3V6 rail before this phase begins.
output_rails.name: 3V6
output_rails.label: VOUT 3.6(V)

fixed_vin_tests._note: VIN test points. expected_vout_v is supplied per rail from the output_rails section above — no need to repeat it here.
